author: feature-implementer
summary: Clamp the /owners page request parameter to the first page. GET /owners?page=0 (and any value below 1) previously built PageRequest.of(page-1, 5) with a negative index; Spring Data rejected it with IllegalArgumentException and the request fell through to the error page. processFindForm now normalizes the parameter once at the request boundary (Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE)), so both the repository query and the currentPage model attribute driving the pager see the clamped value. Covered by OwnerControllerTests.processFindFormWithPageBelowOneShowsFirstPage, which drives page=0 and page=-5 and asserts HTTP 200, the owners/ownersList view, currentPage=1, and a captured Pageable of page index 0.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Same unclamped-page class exists at src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/VetController.java:45 and :61 (`PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize)` on an untrusted `@RequestParam int page`): /vets.html?page=0 still reaches the error page. Pre-existing and outside this change set, so not a finding here — worth a follow-up slice for behavioral parity.
No upper bound on `page` remains (e.g. page=2000000000 yields an empty page). Spring Data computes the offset as a long, so no overflow or query hazard follows; noted only for completeness.
approved_aspects: Untrusted request-boundary value is normalized once, at the boundary, before it reaches either the repository query or the model — no second unclamped path survives (both call sites in processFindForm now pass `currentPage`).

Clamping is total over the int domain: Math.max(page, 1) removes the previous Integer.MIN_VALUE underflow in `page - 1` as well as the negative-index case; no exception path leaks a stack trace or internal state to the client.

No new injection surface: `page` is bound as a primitive int (non-numeric input fails binding before the handler) and reaches Spring Data only as a Pageable, never as query text. The lastName path is unchanged and still uses the derived query findByLastNameStartingWith.
No change to rendered output; `currentPage` is an int model attribute, and Thymeleaf escaping is untouched — no XSS surface added.
No secrets, credentials, tokens, or config values introduced; FIRST_PAGE is a domain constant, not a sensitive value.
Supply chain unchanged: build.gradle, settings.gradle, and gradle/ carry no modifications in this change set, so no new or upgraded dependency to check against NVD.
Test change is test-scope only (ArgumentCaptor plus assertion imports); it adds no production surface and asserts the clamped Pageable index rather than only the HTTP status.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The test body contains a `for (String pageBelowOne : List.of("0", "-5")) { ... }` loop driving two MockMvc calls. testing-principles.md § Assertions bars branching in tests explicitly ('No if/else, switch, or loops. Use collection-aware assertions instead'), and the Agent Decision Checklist's Linearity check (#4) restates it. A loop over boundary values is exactly the case @ParameterizedTest exists for.
findings.fix: Replace the loop with @ParameterizedTest(name = "page={0}") @ValueSource(strings = {"0", "-5"}) (or @ValueSource(ints = {0, -5})) taking the page value as a method parameter, and move the ArgumentCaptor/verify assertions inside the single-invocation body so each parameterized case exercises and asserts one page value in a straight line.

findings.description: testing-principles.md § Test Naming: the BDD naming school (`the{Subject}Should{Outcome}`) applies to tests written or modified from 2026-07-31 onward. This test is new in this slice (added 2026-08-07) and is named after the production method (`processFindForm...`), which is the implementation-name style the brief explicitly rejects as the counter-example ('processFindFormByLastName ... tells a reader nothing about what must be true afterward').
findings.fix: Rename to a behavior-describing name, e.g. `theOwnerSearchShouldClampPageBelowOneToFirstPage`.

findings.description: testing-principles.md § Test Data Construction / Factory Methods: 'tests never call production constructors directly... a slice adding a test writes it behind one [a factory method] from the start.' This new test constructs PageImpl and Owner directly, mirroring the pre-existing (exempted) tests in the file rather than starting the required factory-method vocabulary. Lower priority than the other two findings since no factory exists yet in this suite to reuse, but the brief's rule is unconditional for newly added tests.
findings.fix: Introduce a small factory (e.g. `pageOf(Owner...)`) for the PageImpl construction, or accept as a brief-defect finding if the reviewer/implementer judges retrofitting a factory into an otherwise copy-pasted-style file out of scope for this bug-fix slice.

approved_aspects: Fix correctly clamps at the request boundary once (Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE)) so both the repository query and the currentPage model attribute agree — no duplicated clamping logic
Test drives the fix through real MockMvc dispatch (the sanctioned mock boundary) rather than unit-testing the clamp in isolation, matching the mocking policy
ArgumentCaptor verification on the repository call is a meaningful assertion of the actual Pageable index sent downstream, not just the rendered view
Both documented boundary values (0 and a negative page) are exercised
Build, test, and jacoco all pass; no regression in the existing suite

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Finding 3's decline is not accepted. testing-principles.md#Factory-Methods is not silent or defective here: 'A slice adding a test writes it behind [a factory] from the start.' This test (renamed from processFindFormWithPageBelowOneShowsFirstPage) was added by this same REQ-OWN-002 slice, so it is new code, not the pre-2026-07-31 debt the brief exempts. The implementer's reasoning applies the sibling-test exemption to the wrong test: the seven untouched siblings are correctly exempt as pre-existing debt, but that exemption does not extend to a test this slice itself authored. `new Owner()` on this line is a bare production-constructor call for a Tier 2 (irrelevant) value -- exactly the pattern testing-principles.md's own Tier table flags ('SOME_/ANY_ prefix, or anonymous factory... createAnEmployee()').
findings.fix: Replace `new Owner()` with a small anonymous factory (e.g. `anotherOwner()`) that returns a distinct Owner, so the new test's construction goes through a factory as the brief requires for newly-authored tests. Leaving the PageImpl(...) wrapper as-is is acceptable -- it is a Spring Data framework type, not a production domain constructor the rule targets. No sweep of the seven untouched sibling tests is required.

approved_aspects: Findings 1 and 2 fully applied: the boundary-value loop is now @ParameterizedTest(name = "page={0}") with @ValueSource(ints = {0, -5}), producing two discrete JUnit cases (page=0, page=-5) confirmed in the test XML report; verify() narrowed from times(2) to a single invocation; the captor assertion narrowed from allSatisfy over accumulated captures to a single getPageNumber().isZero() check; method renamed to theOwnerSearchShouldClampPageBelowOneToFirstPage, matching the brief's the{Subject}Should{Outcome} naming school.
./gradlew test passes for OwnerControllerTests with no regressions.
